issues: Dolphin reads as a flat CAD polygon: horizontal scanline fill with hard triangular dorsal fin and tail, no rim light, no phosphor shading gradient, and no clearly visible pectoral fin.
Dolphin is too small and pinned to the top band instead of arcing across the middle 50-60% of the display, so it fails to act as the absolute centerpiece.
Dolphin pose is flat and horizontal rather than a graceful leaping arc, killing the organic 'living creature' feel the reference demands.
Bottom zone (FFT bars + L/R VU blocks + status text) is too bright and heavy; the solid high-contrast cyan FFT rectangles compete with the dolphin for the eye.
Phosphor glow is flat: elements are crisp cyan-on-black with scanlines but lack the soft lit-phosphor halo that sells the OEL look.
Waveform rows are a touch too luminous and tall, edging past the 'subtle, subordinate' brief.
suggestions: Redraw the dolphin as a curved leaping silhouette with a smooth organic outline, add a brighter rim-light edge, an internal phosphor brightness gradient, and a distinct pectoral fin so it looks lit rather than filled.
Scale the dolphin up and recenter it vertically so its arc spans the middle ~55% of the 128px height, making it the unambiguous focal point.
Drop FFT bar brightness and contrast substantially (dimmer, thinner, lower fill) and shrink the VU segments so the bottom strip recedes behind the dolphin.
Add a gentle, tight bloom halo around the dolphin body only — enough to read as glowing phosphor without blowing out the silhouette edges.
Reduce waveform line luminance and clamp the wave band to <=15% of display height so it stays a quiet subordinate layer.
Introduce a short, clean persistence trail behind the dolphin (a few fading ghost frames) to imply motion and reinforce the OEL afterglow character without fogging the whole scene.
